Within that organization, the Network Security team designs and defends the network infrastructure connecting Millennium's global offices, data centers, and cloud environments, spanning perimeter controls such as firewalls, IDS/IPS, NDR, NAC, proxies, email security, and DNS security, as well as the detection and automation stack behind them, including the security data lake, logging pipelines, and SOAR automations. This is a growing organization that combines deep technical expertise with pragmatic risk management to keep pace with the speed and scale of the firm's business. What You'll Do Design, implement, and maintain network security controls, including firewalls, segmentation, secure remote access, intrusion detection and prevention, network detection and response, and network access control, and support secure network architecture for new offices, data centers, and cloud connectivity. Build and maintain the logging pipelines and security data lake that power detection across the environment. Develop, implement, and maintain security policies, procedures, and standards across network security, email security, DNS security, and the security data lake. Strengthen perimeter security through automation, improved monitoring, vulnerability identification, and actionable alerting and reporting. Monitor, manage, and analyze security logs, alerts, and events across multiple systems to identify threats, vulnerabilities, and suspicious activity, and tune network infrastructure to reduce risk while minimizing business disruption. Apply AI to the team's own work, accelerating investigation, automation, detection engineering, and reporting, and help secure the firm's use of AI models, tools, and frameworks. Conduct system audits and vulnerability assessments, manage remediation efforts and findings from audits, penetration tests, and process reviews, participate in incident response for network-related events, and use threat intelligence to sharpen detection, defense, and response. Hands-on experience administering enterprise network security infrastructure, including firewalls, VPN, proxies, intrusion detection and prevention, network detection and response, and network access control, with a practical understanding of proxy engineering concepts. Proven experience as a security engineer with hands-on expertise in logging pipelines, data lakes, or SIEM platforms such as Splunk, ELK, Sentinel, or S3/Athena, plus SOAR automation; experience with breach and attack simulation tooling is a plus. Hands-on AI experience, both using AI tooling in day-to-day security work and securing the use, deployment, and governance of AI models, tools, and frameworks. Strong command of core networking and infrastructure concepts, including TCP/IP, routing, switching, segmentation, DNS, Wi-Fi, and virtualization, along with email and DNS security controls and packet capture and network analysis tools such as tcpdump, Wireshark, or ngrep. Experience securing hybrid on-premises and cloud network architectures, with working knowledge of AWS, GCP, or Azure and proficiency across Windows, Linux, macOS, and container environments such as Docker and Kubernetes. Scripting or development skills in Python, PowerShell, Bash, or similar languages, with the ability to troubleshoot complex network and security issues under time pressure, operate independently in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment, and communicate clearly with both deeply technical teams and senior executive stakeholders. Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cybersecurity/Information Security, or a related field, or commensurate work experience; certifications such as CISSP, GCIA, CISM, CCNP Security, Palo Alto PCNSE, or Fortinet NSE are valued.

full_description: The Faculty of Medicine at the University of Southampton invites applications for a three-year, full-time, fixed-term Research Fellow to join Professor Hanieh Yaghootkar’s interdisciplinary precision-diabetes research programme. Based at University Hospital Southampton, you will investigate the biological mechanisms underlying type 2 diabetes by integrating measures of organ health with large-scale genetic and clinical data. Working alongside genetic epidemiologists, clinicians and data scientists, you will apply advanced statistical and machine learning approaches to identify distinct diabetes subtypes, investigate their genetic determinants and improve prediction of disease risk and progression. The role As a Research Fellow, You Will Develop and apply machine learning approaches to identify distinct subtypes of type 2 diabetes using measures of liver, pancreas, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle health. Characterise the clinical, metabolic and genetic profiles of diabetes subtypes and evaluate their reproducibility across populations. Conduct genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of organ-health traits and diabetes subtypes, and apply Mendelian randomisation to investigate potential causal relationships. Develop and evaluate statistical and machine learning models to predict incident type 2 diabetes and disease progression using genetic and clinical data. Analyse large-scale population datasets, including UK Biobank, using robust statistical methods and reproducible computational workflows. Contribute to high-quality scientific publications, conference presentations and the dissemination of research findings. Collaborate with multidisciplinary researchers across genetic epidemiology, genomics, clinical medicine, imaging, statistics and data science. You will have opportunities to develop your research expertise, contribute to innovative analytical approaches and build your publication record within an internationally collaborative research environment. About You You will have: A PhD in in genetic epidemiology, statistical genetics, biostatistics, data science, computational biology or a closely related discipline. Experience analysing large-scale genetic, epidemiological or biomedical datasets, ideally including UK Biobank. Strong statistical and computational skills, including proficiency in R and/or Python and experience working in Linux-based computing environments. Practical experience conducting GWAS and Mendelian randomisation analyses, including appropriate quality control, sensitivity analyses and interpretation. Experience applying machine learning, clustering, predictive modelling or other advanced statistical methods to complex biomedical data. An understanding of genetic epidemiology and the application of statistical methods to investigate complex disease mechanisms. Evidence of high-quality research outputs, including peer-reviewed publications. Excellent analytical, organisational and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams. Experience with metabolic disease research would be advantageous. What We Can Offer At Southampton, you will join a supportive, internationally connected research environment at the forefront of genetic epidemiology, data science and precision medicine. We offer: Access to large-scale biomedical datasets, high-performance computing infrastructure and secure analytical environments. Opportunities to work at the interface of human genetics, medical imaging, machine learning and metabolic disease research. Collaboration with leading researchers across clinical medicine, genomics, epidemiology and computational science. Opportunities for high-impact publications, scientific conferences, professional development and career progression. A supportive and inclusive working environment committed to equality, diversity and flexible working, including Athena SWAN principles. A competitive University benefits package, including pension provision and generous annual leave. For informal enquiries, contact Professor Hanieh Yaghootkar (h.yaghootkar@soton.ac.uk). full_description: We are seeking an experienced and results-driven PySpark / Big Data Engineer to design, develop, and maintain large-scale batch and real-time data pipelines. In this role, you will be responsible for transforming complex raw data into actionable analytical data models, optimizing distributed computing workloads, and ensuring data integrity, scalability, and security across enterprise data platforms. The ideal candidate possesses deep expertise in Apache Spark architecture, advanced Python programming, distributed systems optimization, modern cloud platforms, and data warehousing/lakehouse paradigms. Key Responsibilities Data Pipeline Design & Development Architect, build, and maintain robust, scalable ETL/ELT pipelines using PySpark and Python to ingest data from diverse batch and streaming sources (Kafka, relational databases, REST APIs, Object Storage). Design and implement Lakehouse architectures using formats such as Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, or Apache Hudi. Build reusable frameworks and data ingestion libraries to standardize enterprise data processing. Spark Performance Tuning & Optimization Diagnose and tune Spark application performance, managing memory allocation, partitions, execution plans, broadcast joins, data skews, and garbage collection. Optimize query execution plans using Catalyst Optimizer and Tungsten execution engine. Monitor and troubleshoot production Spark jobs across cluster management environments (YARN, Kubernetes, or Databricks). Data Modeling & Architecture Collaborate with Data Architects to design dimensional (Star/Snowflake), normalized, and Data Vault schemas optimized for analytical workloads. Ensure efficient data storage, partitioning strategies, and file format selection (Parquet, ORC, Avro). Orchestration, CI/CD & DevOps Schedule and orchestrate complex workflow DAGs using workflow orchestrators such as Apache Airflow, Prefect, or Dagster. Implement CI/CD pipelines (Git, Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions) for automated testing, packaging, and deployment of data pipelines. Write unit tests, integration tests, and data validation routines (e.g., Great Expectations, PyTest). Governance, Security & Quality Implement enterprise data governance, lineage tracking, metadata management, and data quality frameworks. Ensure strict compliance with data security, masking, tokenization, RBAC, and regulatory privacy standards (e.g., GDPR, CCPA). Required Technical Qualifications & Skills Core Technologies - Apache Spark, PySpark (Spark SQL, DataFrames, Datasets, Structured Streaming), Python 3.x Database & Querying - Advanced SQL, Query optimization, Indexing, Window functions Data Lake & Lakehouse - Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, Apache Hudi, Parquet, Avro, ORC Workflow & Orchestration - Apache Airflow, Luigi, Prefect, or Databricks Workflows Cloud Platforms - AWS (EMR, Glue, S3, Redshift), Azure (Synapse, ADLS, HDInsight), or GCP (Dataproc, BigQuery, GCS) Streaming Technologies - Apache Kafka, Spark Structured Streaming, Event Hubs, or Kinesis Key Competencies & Experience Distributed Computing Fundamentals: In-depth knowledge of Spark internals (RDD, Catalyst Optimizer, DAG execution, Shuffling, Narrow vs. Wide dependencies). Production Experience: Minimum 4+ years of hands-on experience building and deploying production-grade PySpark applications at enterprise scale. Problem Solving: Proven track record in debugging memory bottlenecks, Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors, and resolving data skew issues. Data Engineering Best Practices: Experience implementing modular code architectures, logging, monitoring (Prometheus, Grafana, CloudWatch), and alerting. Preferred Qualifications (Nice-to-Have) Hands-on experience with Databricks platform (Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Photon engine, MLflow). Familiarity with Scala/Java in addition to Python. Knowledge of DataOps and Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, CloudFormation). Experience with modern analytical data warehouses (Snowflake, Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift). Relevant certifications: Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate / Professional AWS Certified Data Engineer / Azure Data Engineer Associate (DP-203)CCA Spark and Hadoop Developer (or equivalent) Educational Requirements Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Data Science, or a related quantitative field (or equivalent practical experience). full_description: Role Overview & Objective The Senior IT Business Analyst – Fraud Prevention translates complex, high-level business and risk requirements into detailed, actionable technology deliverables. Serving as the primary bridge between Fraud Operations, Compliance, Risk Management, and Technology engineering teams, you will leverage modern analysis methodologies and enterprise AI capabilities to define, design, and implement advanced fraud detection and mitigation solutions. Your contributions will directly strengthen organizational resilience against emerging fraud threats while ensuring a frictionless customer journey. Key Responsibilities Requirements Engineering & Business Analysis Leverage enterprise collaboration intelligence and AI-assisted elicitation tools to structure stakeholder workshops, extract business rules from discussions, and resolve requirement ambiguities and edge-case exceptions with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs). Elicit, analyze, and document comprehensive functional and non-functional requirements, producing industry-standard Business Requirement Documents (BRDs), Functional Requirement Documents (FRDs), and technical specifications. Utilize advanced analytical tools for requirement pattern discovery and dependency mapping across distributed systems. Design and maintain robust process artifacts—including use case models, activity diagrams, sequence diagrams, system context diagrams, and Business Process Model and Notation (BPMN 2.0) workflows—covering standard operating paths, fraud-positive scenarios, false-positive handling, timeouts, vendor outages, and dual-control approvals. Define detailed technical and integration requirements for in-house detection engines, third-party vendor platforms, and core payment rails (e.g., Card Authorization, ACH, Wire, Real-Time Payments [RTP]). Decompose business initiatives into structured Jira Epics and INVEST-compliant User Stories featuring testable Gherkin syntax (Given-When-Then) acceptance criteria across diverse personas Establish and maintain end-to-end Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) linking regulatory/policy mandates to BRDs, FRDs, user stories, test cases, and compliance audit evidence. Facilitate backlog grooming and sprint planning in Jira, ensuring user stories meet the Definition of Ready (DoR) and align with engineering sprint capacity. AI-Powered Fraud Solution Design Translate evolving fraud typologies—such as Account Takeover (ATO), Authorized Push Payment (APP) fraud, Synthetic Identity Theft, and mule account networks—into functional and technical specifications for machine learning models and real-time rule engines. Perform comprehensive impact assessments and root-cause analyses on fraud policy and rule updates, balancing fraud capture rate optimization against customer friction and False Positive Rates (FPR). System Integration & Testing Serve as the core technical liaison across core banking engines, fraud decisioning platforms, case management workflows, and identity verification/biometric APIs. Define data mapping specifications, schema definitions (JSON/XML), and API payloads for real-time transaction screening, event streaming (e.g., Kafka), and batch monitoring. Formulate and execute User Acceptance Testing (UAT) strategies, detailed test scripts, and defect triage workflows to validate fraud detection efficacy and system reliability prior to production releases. Required Qualifications & Experience Education & Experience Education: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Management Information Systems (MIS), Finance, Business Analytics, or a related discipline. Enterprise Fraud & Risk Platforms: Practical experience with market-leading fraud detection and decisioning engines.
